exposure: external cephalic version (ECV) for the leading twin (twin A) in breech presentation
cohort: 23 women with confirmed dichorionic-diamniotic twin pregnancy from the 35th completed week of pregnancy
finding: External cephalic version (ECV) for the leading twin in breech presentation in dichorionic and diamniotic twin pregnancies without the use of regional anesthetics and tocolysis was successful in 56% of cases and resulted in a significant increase in the spontaneous vaginal delivery rate for both twins and a significant reduction in blood loss at delivery.
mod_finding: The spontaneous vaginal delivery rate for both twins was significantly higher in the successful ECV group (95%) compared to the group where ECV was not successful (12.5%).
